LayoutEditor__RenderComposites__Meta.Meta__Description: One row per layer that goes into the picture a viewport shows: what it is called, whether it means anything on a 3D viewport, whether it carries a toggle, and - new in 1.0.0 - how thick its lines are. The Render Composites panel is built from this file, so adding a composite is a config edit.
LayoutEditor__RenderComposites__Meta.Meta__WhyWeightsHere: Before v2.27.0 the outline on a 2D backing picture was drawn at 1.0 px - the drawing view config's built-in fallback - one number for every viewport on every sheet. Na__AppConfig__Main.json did carry RenderEffect__ProfileLines__Drawing2dEdgeWidth 0.55, and it was read as the bake width, but TrueVision never registered the main config with the drawing view (closed 13-Sep-2026), so 0.55 only ever reached the live floor plan and elevation views. The bake width is now Composite__Weight on the profileLinework row below, defaulting to the 1.0 every existing sheet was baked at, and a single viewport can override it.
LayoutEditor__RenderComposites__Meta.Meta__WeightKinds: factor = a multiplier on the sheet's master viewport lineweight (Sheet__Lineweights.ViewportPt), so the drawing keeps its hierarchy when the master moves. pixels = a real pixel count in the render buffer, which is what a screen-space effect actually consumes. percent = how much of a post pass is applied, 0 being none of it and 100 all of it - a dial, not a width. none = this composite draws no line and gets no control; the row is still listed so the file is a complete inventory rather than a selective one.
LayoutEditor__RenderComposites__Meta.Meta__PerViewport: A viewport stores an override only for a weight it has actually been given, in Viewport__CompositeWeights. Everything untouched reads this file, so changing a default here moves every viewport that never disagreed.
LayoutEditor__RenderComposites__Meta.Meta__WeightTwoDOnly: Weight__TwoDOnly marks a weight that only applies to a 2D viewport even though the composite's toggle also means something in 3D. The profile outline on a 3D viewport is the 3D composer's distance-scaled effect, with its own width in Na__AppConfig__Main.json; this weight sets the fixed 2D Sobel width only.
LayoutEditor__RenderComposites__Meta.Meta__BaseImageWeight: New in 1.1.0 (13-Sep-2026). The base image's weight is the width of the model's own edges - the SketchUp linework the loader upgrades to fat lines, drawn everywhere else at RenderConfig__Linework__LineWidth (0.8) in Na__AppConfig__Main.json. The snapshot renderer sets it for one render and hands every edge material its own width back, so the live 3D view never moves. From 1.2.0 (19-Sep-2026) the default is 2.00, deliberately heavier than that live-view global - a viewport nobody has touched now reads noticeably bolder than the raw scene, on screen and in the PDF bake alike, since both read this same default. three.js resolves a fat line against the renderer's viewport on every draw, so like the section outline this is a true pixel count in the buffer being rendered.
LayoutEditor__RenderComposites__Meta.Meta__EnhanceStrength: New in 1.3.0 (20-Sep-2026). Enhance Whitecard is the first weight whose kind is percent. It is not a line width at all - it is how far the levels and sharpen pass is taken, 0 leaving the render exactly as it came out of the renderer and 100 being the full pass the style has always applied. In between, the levels white point travels from 255 down to Enhance.LevelsWhite, the black point up from 0, the gamma away from 1.0 and the sharpen opacity up from nothing, so the dial is continuous rather than a set of presets. The default is 100 on purpose: every sheet ever baked reads exactly as it did, and a viewport only softens once someone says so.
LayoutEditor__RenderComposites__Meta.Meta__DepthFog: New in 1.4.0 (20-Sep-2026). Depth Fog is the first composite that sits OVER the projected linework rather than under it, which is why its Order is the lowest in the file - the panel lists layers front to back. It is a toggle with no weight. The fog ITSELF is not set here: where it starts, where it is full and how hard it comes on belong to the drawing (Elevation__DepthFog, set in Dev Tools > Elevations), because they are distances behind that drawing's plane and must not be set twice. This row only says whether THIS viewport shows its drawing's fog, and it is on by default - a drawing's fog is off until its author switches it on, so ticked means 'follow the drawing'. The fog is rendered as an image of its own with the fog in its alpha, laid over the vectors in the frame and in the PDF; it never enters the base image or its key.
LayoutEditor__RenderComposites__Meta.Meta__KeyStability: Composite__Key is what saved viewports already hold and must not be renamed. baseImage is labelled Context Layer for exactly this reason - see the note in Na__LayoutEditor__Panel__Styles__.js.

LayoutEditor__RenderComposites__Layers.Composite__Note: The drawing's own depth fog, laid over the linework so far lines fade with far surfaces. Ticked follows the drawing: nothing shows until the drawing's fog is switched on, and its three values are set, in Dev Tools > Elevations. Untick to show this one viewport bare.

The exact vector drawing over the picture. Its weight multiplies every class AND every per-category factor, so it is the one number that thickens or thins the whole vector drawing in this viewport without touching the sheet master.

The screen-space silhouette found by the Sobel pass on the backing render - the layer that stops a curved wall reading as a blank patch. Measured in pixels of that buffer at the real output resolution (v2.25.0 resized it per tile; before that a baked sheet found its outline at viewport resolution and stretched it).

The inked edge of cut material on the backing render, drawn by the section mesh overlay. It has no toggle of its own - a drawing either has a cut or it has not - but it does have a weight, and a heavy cut line is most of what makes a plan read as a plan.

What the occluders covered, drawn dashed. Its weight multiplies the hidden class only, on top of the projected linework weight, so hidden work can be quietened without thinning anything that is actually visible.
Transparent materials occlude like walls. Changes what is drawn, not how thickly.
Materials replaced with white card. A shading choice; no linework of its own.

Levels and sharpen over the finished raster so whitecard greys reach paper white. A post pass on pixels, so its number is not a line width but how much of the pass to apply: 0 leaves the render untouched, 100 is the full effect.

The rendered picture everything else is drawn over - the layer furthest back. Off leaves the vector drawing alone on the paper. Its weight is how thick the model's own edges draw inside that picture - the SketchUp linework, not the projected vectors over it - on a 2D and a 3D viewport alike. The key stays baseImage so every saved viewport keeps its meaning.

LayoutEditor__RenderComposites__Fallback.Fallback__Description: A composite key a saved viewport holds that this file does not list keeps working as a plain toggle with no weight, rather than vanishing from the panel.
